# Running the Code {#sec-running-the-code}

All the code in this book runs inside one container image. It contains Python,
NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, JupyterLab, Quarto and LaTeX. The only thing you need
on your computer is [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/get-docker/)
(on Windows, Docker Desktop with Linux containers).

If you just want to experiment with a single example, the *Try it* boxes in the
HTML edition run in your browser and need nothing at all.

## Get the source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/antoniofloresgil/digitalsignalprocessing.git
cd digitalsignalprocessing
```

## Option 1: JupyterLab

```sh
make lab
```

Then open <http://localhost:8888>. The repository is mounted at `/work`, so
anything you save there is kept on your computer. Each chapter is a `.qmd`
file: you can copy its code cells into a notebook, or open the chapter with the
Quarto extension and run cells one by one.

Without `make` (for example in Windows PowerShell), build and run the image
directly:

```sh
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f docker/Dockerfile -t dsp-book:dev .
docker run --rm -it --platform linux/amd64 --env HOME=/tmp --publish 127.0.0.1:8888:8888 --mount "type=bind,source=${PWD},target=/work" dsp-book:dev jupyter lab --ip 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 --no-browser --ServerApp.token=''
```

## Option 2: VS Code dev container

Install the *Dev Containers* extension, open the repository folder and choose
**Reopen in Container**. VS Code builds the same image and runs inside it, with
Python, Jupyter and Quarto ready to use. Open any chapter and use
*Run Cell* on its code blocks.

## Option 3: build the whole book

```sh
make render      # HTML and PDF in _book/
make preview     # live preview at http://localhost:4200
```

Building the book runs every code cell, so a successful build is also a test
that all the examples work.

## What is in the image

| Component | Version | Used for |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| Ubuntu | 24.04 (pinned by digest) | Base system |
| Quarto | 1.10.19 (pinned by hash) | Building the book |
| Python | 3.12 | Running the examples |
| NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib | see `docker/requirements.txt` | Computation and plots |
| JupyterLab | see `docker/requirements.txt` | Interactive work |
| TeX Live (XeLaTeX) | Ubuntu 24.04 packages | PDF edition |

The in-browser examples use [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org), a build of Python
for WebAssembly. It provides NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib too, but its versions
may differ slightly from the container's.
